conviction_note: The findings sum to 0.0. A mechanical revenue shortfall against a disputed bar and below-spot call exercises are offset by a likely headline GAAP profit from the bitcoin remeasurement and by a crowded short at the 52-week low. p_up is 51 on an 8% absolute move, so the scaled number is +0.16. findings.finding: Q4 FY26 bitcoin-mining revenue computes to about $121M from the company's own monthly updates: July 586 BTC × Luxor July average $63,708, plus August 593 × $69,263, plus September 529 × $80,386. That is about 4% below Benzinga's $126.3M and 7% below its $130.6M. In Q3 the same production-times-average-price method matches the reported $138.0M at the CFO's stated ~$72k revenue per BTC (≈1,917 BTC).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue was a narrow miss on each of the last three prints. Q1 FY26 (2026-02-05): $181.2M vs $195.5M, -9% after hours, yet the window closed +21.96% as bitcoin rebounded (https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/clsk-shares-decline-after-hours-on-disappointing-q1-earnings/cZbZFWyR4na/amp). Q3 FY26 (2026-08-06): $138.0M vs $142.2M, window -3.53%. Q4 FY25: miss, after-hours dip, window +13.79%. A revenue miss gets sold after hours and then gets swamped by bitcoin beta.
findings.why_not_priced: Every input is public: August update 2026-09-08 (https://finviz.com/news/389855/cleanspark-releases-august-2026-operational-update), July update 2026-08-05 (https://finviz.com/news/377574/cleanspark-releases-july-2026-operational-update), and Luxor's monthly averages. A desk that has done the arithmetic already has it. But the vendor consensus shown ($126-131M) still sits above it, which suggests the published bar has not caught up. If the market had fully reconciled, the vendor consensus would read about $121M.
findings.independence: Luxor's July, August and September 2026 lookbacks are a separate source for the price input (https://hashrateindex.com/blog/luxor-hashrate-lookback-series-september-2026/, https://hashrateindex.com/blog/luxor-hashrate-lookback-series-august-2026/). The Q3 calibration comes from the Q3 FY26 call transcript (https://s21.q4cdn.com/978676932/files/doc_financials/2026/q3/Q3FY26-Financial-Results-Transcript.pdf). Production comes from the company's own documents.

findings.finding: Q4 GAAP net income is very likely positive, because the quarter carries a large favourable bitcoin mark-to-market. BTC went from about $59-60k on 2026-06-30 to about $83.6k on 2026-09-30, a 39-44% quarter (https://cryptobriefing.com/bitcoin-q3-up-44-best-quarter/). Holdings were 13,924 BTC at June and 13,530 at September. That is roughly +$300M+ of remeasurement, against Q3's -$133M. The result sets a headline GAAP EPS likely above +$0.30 against Benzinga's -$0.37.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This line gets a headline reaction from algos after hours, and the fundamentals then ignore it. On Q1 FY26 a GAAP loss driven by the mark, -$1.35 vs -$0.15, sent the stock -9% after hours. Peers this season: MARA posted $634M net profit almost all from bitcoin gains and was 'little changed' after hours (https://theblock.co/news/business/2026-11-09-mara-q3-earnings-net-profit-bitcoin-sale-ai-pivot-436950). RIOT posted +$0.01 vs -$0.34 and rose ~14.6%, but that print carried a $28B Corsicana lease (https://finviz.com/news/415563/riot-platforms-beats-on-a-thin-profit-but-the-28-billion-corsicana-lease-is-the-real-story-as-funding-questions-linger).
findings.why_not_priced: The bitcoin path is public, so the economics are priced. What may not be priced is the headline: the Benzinga EPS bar of -$0.37 does not reflect a 40% bitcoin quarter. If the market fully expected the gain, the vendor EPS consensus would be positive. Chartmill's FY -$3.80 implies a Q4 near -$0.04, so part of the street has updated, which is why this is sized small. Offsets that could shrink it: a fiscal-year-end miner or goodwill impairment (hashprice was near a record low in June-July), derivative losses, and deferred tax.
findings.independence: Quarter-end prices come from several outlets (https://www.simplemining.io/insights/post/bitcoin-market-report-september-2026). MARA's same-quarter $885M digital-asset gain is the peer confirmation (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001507605/000150760526000026/q326shareholderletter.htm). This finding shares the Q3 release with finding 1 only for the share count and the Q3 base.

findings.finding: The digital-asset-management line, which the CFO credited with $25.8M of fiscal-year cash returns and sales '7% greater than spot' in Q3, turned in Q4. In August 500 BTC were called away and the average sale price was $65,420 against a monthly average of $69,263. In September 700 BTC were called away and the average was $72,928 against $80,386. That is sales 6-9% below spot, plus derivative losses on short calls in a +40% bitcoin quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None isolated. Management has used this line as a quality point on calls (Q3 transcript p.6).
findings.why_not_priced: The sale prices are in the monthly updates, but nobody aggregates them into a quarterly derivative result. It will first appear as a P&L line and as a talking point the CFO can no longer use. If it were priced, previews would mention a hedging loss, and none found does.
findings.independence: The September figures are in a separate document, the September update (https://finviz.com/news/400827/cleanspark-releases-september-2026-operational-update). The monthly average prices come from Luxor (https://hashrateindex.com/blog/luxor-hashrate-lookback-series-september-2026/).

findings.finding: The call is the first company read on Texas since the Nov 3 election of Gina Hinojosa as governor, who campaigned for a data-center moratorium. The Sandersville tenant holds exclusivity over up to 885 MW at Sealy and Brazoria but has signed no Texas lease. The stock fell 11% and 17% on Nov 4-5. KBW downgraded to market perform with a $9.50 target; Bernstein cut its target to $11 from $24 and expects the Texas pause to last. The direction of the call's Texas commentary (a lease, an extension of exclusivity, or the tenant walking) is unknown.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Tenant news is what this stock trades on. The July 2026 Sandersville lease and Texas exclusivity drove an up-move (https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/07/14/why-cleanspark-stock-climbed-today/). Texas policy drove -26% in two sessions in November. In Nov 2025 the focus was the CFO's tenant-onboarding comment, not the revenue miss.
findings.why_not_priced: The bad news is priced: the stock is -39% in 20 days, 2% above its 52-week low, with put skew at +13. What is not priced is the company's answer. On the Q3 call (2026-08-06) the CEO said the Texas exclusivity 'remains intact' with 'no anticipated change to our energization time lines' and that a replacement tenant would rush in if this one fell out. In October he said demand 'remains relentless'. Neither statement addresses the new governor.
findings.independence: The Q3 call transcript gives management's prior Texas framing (https://s21.q4cdn.com/978676932/files/doc_financials/2026/q3/Q3FY26-Financial-Results-Transcript.pdf). A second TIKR article covers the Nov 4-5 moves (https://www.tikr.com/blog/cleanspark-sinks-another-17-iren-down-17-as-bitcoin-tumbles-and-ai-data-center-selloff-deepens). Both TIKR pieces are from one publisher.

The stock is down 18.6% over 5 days and 38.9% over 20, at 2.35% above its 52-week low. Any benign headline, such as the GAAP profit in finding 2 or a Texas update, has a squeeze mechanism behind it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Feb 2026 print went from -9% after hours to a +21.96% window. The Nov 2025 print went from an after-hours dip to +13.79%. On this name, after-hours reads have reversed upward twice.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is visible to everyone and is part of the price. It is filed because it shapes the reaction function, not as unpriced information. Puts bid at +13 skew mean the option market is leaning the other way.
findings.independence: Massive.com's 2026-10-30 settlement shows 78.73M shares and 4.6 days to cover (https://massive.com/quote/CLSK). Mid-2026 data showed ~33% of float (https://altindex.com/ticker/clsk/short-interest).

findings.finding: In September 2026 a subsidiary closed $2.276B of 7.875% senior secured notes due 2031, which the company says fully funds Sandersville through completion without dilution. Long-term debt was $1.78B at June 30, before these notes. The money buys the $6.6B, 20-year triple-net lease build, with expected NOI of about $330M a year, long-lead items prepaid and RFS in Q4 CY2027.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None at a print. The financing was announced in September (8-K Items 1.01/2.03, 2026-09-25).
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced; it was announced and filed. The new item at the print is the first P&L and balance-sheet view: interest carry of about $179M a year, partly capitalised, against mining gross profit that does not cover miner depreciation ($52.5M vs $99.9M in Q3).
findings.independence: EDGAR filing index shows the 8-K Items 1.01 and 2.03 on 2026-09-25 (https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0000827876&type=&dateb=&owner=include&count=40). This shares the September-update document with finding 3.

outside_window.finding: Governor-elect Hinojosa takes office on 2027-01-19. Any actual Texas pause on data-center approvals lands after this window.

Bitcoin fell from about $83.6k at fiscal-year end to about $63.7k on 2026-11-19, which implies a large mark-to-market loss in Q1 FY27 (reported in February 2027). The call may disclose it as a subsequent event, but the P&L impact lands after this window.

baseline_tension: Mixed. The revenue shortfall and the call-exercise losses agree with the +13 put skew and the -39% run-up, so they are likely priced. The headline GAAP profit and the 43%-of-float short cut against the skew. The net is about zero, so p_up stays near 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (disputed bar): Benzinga shows $126.3M and $130.6M, and the EPS bar is -$0.37 vs about -$0.04 implied by Chartmill, so every size is capped small. The revenue finding went from -0.8 to -0.6.

Lesson 2 (one-offs): the bitcoin remeasurement is below operating income with no path to guidance, so the GAAP-profit finding went from +0.8 to +0.4. The derivative finding went from -0.4 to -0.3 for the same reason.
Lesson 4 (financing is a question): the $2.276B notes fund a signed $6.6B triple-net lease build with prepaid long-lead items, so the sign went from -0.2 to 0.0.
Lesson 7 (crowded short): the +0.5 positioning finding is left standing, and no negative was sized up against a 43%-of-float short.

Rebuilt base rate (sweep flag): the baseline's reaction dates 2026-08-06, 2026-05-11, 2026-02-05 and 2025-11-25 match confirmed earnings releases (Q3, Q2, Q1 and FY25 documents), not monthly updates, so the history was used for abs_move_pct.
The Texas (0.0) finding and abs_move_pct (8.0) were left unchanged.
